concepts.title: Classification of 2-D and 3-D Shapes
concepts.definition: Two-dimensional (2-D) shapes are flat plane figures with only length and breadth, whereas three-dimensional (3-D) shapes are solid objects occupying space with length, breadth, and height or depth.
concepts.key_idea: Plane figures have two dimensions, while solid shapes have three dimensions.
question_patterns: classify the given figure as 2-D or 3-D
is a circle a two-dimensional or three-dimensional shape
identify whether a cylinder is a plane figure or a solid shape
distinguish between 2-D and 3-D objects

solution_steps.action: Analyze the dimensions of the object
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the object is flat (having only length and breadth) or occupies space (having length, breadth, and depth/height).

solution_steps.action: Classify the shape
solution_steps.explain: If it is flat, it is a 2-D plane figure. If it has depth/height, it is a 3-D solid shape.

concepts.title: Faces, Edges, and Vertices of Solids
concepts.definition: A solid shape is bounded by flat surfaces called faces; the line segments where two faces meet are edges, and the corner points where edges meet are vertices.
concepts.key_idea: Faces are 2-D surfaces, edges are 1-D line segments, and vertices are 0-D points.
question_patterns: find the number of faces, edges, and vertices of a cube
how many vertices does a triangular pyramid have
identify the faces, edges, and vertices of a cuboid
count the corners and flat surfaces of a solid

solution_steps.action: Count the flat surfaces (faces)
solution_steps.explain: Identify and count all the flat boundary surfaces of the given solid.

solution_steps.action: Count the boundary line segments (edges)
solution_steps.explain: Identify and count all the line segments where two faces intersect.

solution_steps.action: Count the corner points (vertices)
solution_steps.explain: Identify and count all the points where three or more edges meet.

concepts.title: Nets of 3-D Solids
concepts.definition: A net is a two-dimensional skeleton outline of a solid shape that can be folded along its edges to construct the three-dimensional object.
concepts.key_idea: Folding a 2-D net along its shared boundaries reconstructs a 3-D solid.
question_patterns: identify the net of a cube
which of the following nets can be folded to form a cylinder
match the given net with its corresponding 3-D solid
can this net form a tetrahedron

solution_steps.action: Analyze the 2-D net structure
solution_steps.explain: Count the number of faces in the net and examine their shapes (e.g., six squares for a cube).

solution_steps.action: Simulate folding the net
solution_steps.explain: Check if folding the faces along the edges causes any overlaps or leaves any open gaps.

solution_steps.action: Identify the resulting solid
solution_steps.explain: If it folds perfectly without overlaps or gaps, match it with the corresponding 3-D shape.

concepts.title: Opposite Face Values of a Standard Die
concepts.definition: A standard die is a cube where the numbers on any two opposite faces always add up to seven.
concepts.key_idea: The sum of dots on opposite faces of a standard die is always 7.
question_patterns: find the number on the opposite face of a die when the top face is
what is the value of the opposite face of
calculate the opposite face of a die showing
if a die shows a face value of, what is on the bottom face

solution_steps.action: Subtract the given face value from 7
solution_steps.explain: Since the sum of opposite faces on a standard die is 7, the opposite face is 7 minus the given face value.

concepts.title: Oblique and Isometric Sketches
concepts.definition: Oblique sketches are 2-D representations of solids where lengths are not proportional but convey the visual appearance, whereas isometric sketches are drawn on dot paper with proportional, exact measurements.
concepts.key_idea: Isometric sketches preserve proportional measurements, while oblique sketches do not.
question_patterns: draw an oblique sketch of a cube
what is the difference between an oblique sketch and an isometric sketch
sketch a cuboid on an isometric dot sheet
represent a solid on a flat surface using isometric dot paper

solution_steps.action: Identify the type of sketch required
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the drawing needs to have exact proportional measurements (isometric) or just a visual representation (oblique).

solution_steps.action: Verify the properties of the sketch
solution_steps.explain: For an isometric sketch, ensure parallel lines are drawn along the dot grid directions and lengths match the given dimensions.

concepts.title: Dimensions of Combined Cubes Placed Side-by-Side
concepts.definition: When multiple identical cubes are placed side-by-side in a single row, they form a cuboid whose length increases proportionally with the number of cubes, while the breadth and height remain equal to the side length of a single cube.
concepts.key_idea: Only the dimension along the direction of placement increases; other dimensions remain unchanged.
question_patterns: if two cubes of side ... are placed side by side, find the dimensions of the resulting cuboid
calculate the length, breadth, and height of a cuboid formed by joining ... cubes of edge ... side by side
what are the dimensions of the cuboid when ... cubes of side ... are placed in a row
find the resulting dimensions of placing ... cubes of side ... together

solution_steps.action: Calculate the length of the resulting cuboid
solution_steps.explain: The length is the product of the number of cubes and the side length of one cube.

solution_steps.action: Determine the breadth of the resulting cuboid
solution_steps.explain: The breadth remains equal to the side length of a single cube.

solution_steps.action: Determine the height of the resulting cuboid
solution_steps.explain: The height remains equal to the side length of a single cube.

concepts.title: Cross-Sections of Solids via Slicing
concepts.definition: A cross-section is the 2-D shape obtained by cutting or slicing a 3-D solid either vertically (perpendicular to the base) or horizontally (parallel to the base).
concepts.key_idea: Slicing a solid yields a 2-D plane figure as a cross-section.
question_patterns: what cross-section do you get when you give a vertical cut to a brick
find the horizontal cross-section of a circular pipe
describe the shape of the slice of an ice cream cone
what shape results from a horizontal cut of a round apple

solution_steps.action: Identify the orientation of the cut
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the cut is vertical (perpendicular to the base) or horizontal (parallel to the base).

solution_steps.action: Visualize the intersection plane
solution_steps.explain: Determine the shape of the boundary where the cutting plane intersects the solid.

solution_steps.action: Name the resulting 2-D shape
solution_steps.explain: Identify the 2-D geometric figure formed by the cross-section (e.g., circle, square, rectangle, triangle).

concepts.title: Shadows of 3-D Objects
concepts.definition: A shadow is a 2-D projection of a 3-D solid onto a flat screen when illuminated by a light source, with its shape depending on the orientation of the solid and the position of the light.
concepts.key_idea: Shadows represent 3-D shapes projected into 2-D space.
question_patterns: what is the shape of the shadow of a ball under a bulb
can a cube cast a shadow in the shape of a hexagon
identify the solid that casts a circular shadow
describe the shadow of a cylindrical pipe when the light is directly above it

solution_steps.action: Analyze the position of the light source relative to the solid
solution_steps.explain: Determine the direction from which the light rays hit the solid.

solution_steps.action: Project the outline of the solid onto the screen
solution_steps.explain: Visualize the 2-D boundary formed by blocking the light rays.

solution_steps.action: Determine the shape of the shadow
solution_steps.explain: Identify the 2-D shape of the resulting shadow.

concepts.title: Multi-Angle Views of Solids
concepts.definition: A 3-D solid can be observed from different directions to produce distinct 2-D views: the front view, the side view, and the top view.
concepts.key_idea: Looking at a solid from different orthogonal angles provides a set of 2-D views that describe its 3-D structure.
question_patterns: draw the top view of the given solid
identify the front, side, and top views of the building
what does the side view of a cylinder look like
match the views with the corresponding solid

solution_steps.action: Select the viewing direction
solution_steps.explain: Choose whether to look at the solid from directly in front, from the side, or from directly above.

solution_steps.action: Project the visible faces onto a 2-D plane
solution_steps.explain: Disregard depth and draw only the flat shapes visible from that specific direction.

solution_steps.action: Identify the resulting 2-D view
solution_steps.explain: Label the drawn shape as the front, side, or top view.
